To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ethics of organizing compassionate support for employees during the Brisbane flood crisis were contingent on the entanglement of social and material processes; (2) the ethics of compassion were constituted in the materiality of technology and organizational routines; (3) compassionate support was contingent on the temporal processes of sociomaterality; and (4) compassionate support for flood-affected employees was substantiated or negated by the entanglement and disentanglement of social processes and materiality.
compassion is a variable state that emerges from the entanglement of social and material phenomena in temporal processes.
the ethics of compassionate organizing are contingent on the sociomateriality of the situation and that compassion can become a resource for organizational resilience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
what happens to compassion when it is mobilized in organizational settings.
how the ethics of compassion are enacted through the entanglement of material and social processes.
how the ethics of compassion are constituted in the context of a flood crisis, and what happens when organizations respond to a crisis in a compassionate manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ethics of compassion is a variable state that can be substantiated and substantively changed by the sociomateriality of the situation.
the ethics of compassion are contingent and emergent, and that they are entangled with social relations, materiality, and the phenomenological experience of the event.

compassionate support provided by an organization to its employees during and after a flood crisis is contingent upon the sociomaterial entanglements that are present at the time of the crisis and the time that it takes to respond.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how compassion is a variable state that emerges in the context of sociomaterial processes.
the ethics of compassion are constituted in the sociomaterial relations of a river flooding and organizations responding.
the ethics of compassionate organizing are contingent upon the social and the physical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ethics of compassionate organizing are not fixed but are variable and contingent on the social, material and corporeal.
compassion is not just an emotion or an ethic, but also a sociomaterial process.
the social is not a separate realm from the material.
